Over the last two decades, many new parties have emerged in
Western Europe. The emergence of new parties is not a novelty, but their number and electoral success, especially in
some countries, are particularly relevant during this period
(Chiaramonte & Emanuele, 2022). Apparently, some of these
parties, at least in their first stage, have bet on increasing their
internal democracy to reconnect with disaffected citizens by
leaning on digital tools. Nevertheless, many authors point
out that these parties are subject to electoral competition and
become institutionalized, a fact that makes them take steps
back in terms of internal democracy (for instance, Meloni &
Lupato, 2023). Some scholars also claim that their participation model is essentially plebiscitary (the what, how, and when
of what is discussed or asked remain in the hands of an elite),
